web-content-fb16b19b0ae4.e3b5093454a7073: Every live show and 1:1 session on avaTOK is priced
web-content-fb16b19b0ae4.a87735d60214c6b: , in whole tokens. avaTOK uses 100 Tokens = $1 as an internal accounting anchor. Buyers see a server-owned local-currency quote at checkout, with the quote and payment snapshot recorded immutably.
web-content-fb16b19b0ae4.ec3114ff3bbd851: When you create or edit a listing, you enter a whole-number token price for one hour with one participant. The buyer pays that listing price for each booking or ticket, plus GST, at checkout.
web-content-fb16b19b0ae4.4c3068bb408b798: There's a floor: avaTOK won't accept a price below
web-content-fb16b19b0ae4.ad6755a60d527e8: for a paid live show or 1:1 session. The wizard and the server both refuse anything lower.
web-content-fb16b19b0ae4.d77acc9a97355e9: Marketplace listings (buy, sell, social items) don't carry this per-hour structure or floor — you set a plain price for the item or offer.
web-content-fb16b19b0ae4.5a37f32bc67133d: There's a "this is a free show" option in the listing wizard, but as things stand it's restricted to test accounts. On a regular creator account, turning it on and trying to publish will be refused — you'll need to set a price to go live.
web-content-fb16b19b0ae4.483825a086e92a7: Your listing price is shown in tokens. At checkout, the server supplies the local-currency quote and records the immutable quote/payment snapshot. Do not describe the internal anchor as a fixed local-currency conversion.
web-content-fb16b19b0ae4.29e372cea92f4ea: avaTOK keeps a fee out of what a buyer pays; you don't see it as a separate deduction when setting your price, but it does affect what you actually receive. See
web-content-fb16b19b0ae4.6f124894575da43: You can edit a listing's price after it's published, the same way you'd edit any other detail from
web-content-fb16b19b0ae4.324551df81803db: . Enter a whole number of tokens — the server always rounds down to the nearest whole token, so there's no such thing as a fractional price.
